is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae (s.l.) vectors in Nigeria (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) (Abstract, page 1; Tables 2 and 3, pages 6-7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 2 and 3 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for Ace-1 and kdr (L1014F) across different study locations (pages 6-7).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae/pupae from field sites in five states in South-East Nigeria (Methods, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collection and laboratory analysis (Methods, pages 2-4).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides specific locations (LGA and village/town names) and coordinates for the collection sites (Methods, page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted from April to December 2016 (Methods, page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections conducted in 2016.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is included in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the insecticide resistance status and underlying mechanisms (kdr L1014F and Ace-1 G119S) of Anopheles gambiae (s.l.) in five states of South-East Nigeria. Mosquitoes were collected in 2016 and tested against four classes of insecticides. High frequencies of the L1014F mutation were found across the zone, while the G119S mutation was detected at low frequency only in Ebonyi State.
